subject: Business
title: S-Curves of Technology Adoption
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: S-Curves of Technology Adoption.

hook.text: Smartphones went from novelty to necessity in about seven years. The curve is always the same shape.

buildup.text: Technology adoption follows an S-curve: slow start, rapid acceleration, and eventual plateau.

discovery.text: The slow start fools incumbents into thinking the threat is small. By the time acceleration hits, it's too late.

twist.text: Companies often invest at the top of one S-curve instead of the bottom of the next one.

climax.text: Successful firms jump to the next S-curve before the current one peaks. Intel did it across chip generations.

punchline.text: Ride the curve up. But start building the next one early.

quiz.question: What mistake do incumbents often make with S-curves?
options: They invest at the top of the current curve instead of the bottom of the next
They adopt new technology too quickly
They always jump to the next curve too early

details.summary: Technology adoption follows an S-curve pattern: slow initial uptake, rapid growth through the mainstream, and gradual flattening as the market saturates. New S-curves emerge as successor technologies begin their own adoption cycles, eventually replacing incumbents.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding where your technology sits on the S-curve informs strategic investment timing. Companies that ride the inflection point of a new S-curve grow exponentially, while those that invest in flattening curves face diminishing returns.
takeaways: Technology adoption follows an S-shaped curve from launch to saturation
The inflection point is where adoption accelerates most rapidly
New S-curves emerge as successor technologies replace plateauing ones

faq.question: How can a company tell where it is on the S-curve?
faq.answer: Slow growth in a nascent market suggests the early flat portion. Accelerating adoption with mainstream customer interest indicates the steep middle. Declining growth rates with market saturation signal the top. Track adoption rate changes, not absolute numbers.

faq.question: What should a company do when its technology approaches the top of its S-curve?
faq.answer: Invest in the next S-curve technology before the current one plateaus. Milk the existing product for cash while funding next-generation development. The hardest part is cannibalizing a profitable current product to fund an uncertain successor. But waiting too long is worse.
